claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by competition between thermodynamic and kinetic factors.
First-principles calculations can predict the phase stability of this alloy using composition, temperature, and processing conditions as key parameters.
Variations in composition, temperature, and processing conditions alter constituent phases and transformation behavior.
Thermodynamic and kinetic factors influence phase formation and evolution.
Phase stability across the relevant thermal regime is connected to composition-dependent thermodynamic instability.
Prior studies did not provide a predictive explanation of phase stability or connect it to composition-dependent thermodynamic instability.
Agreement between calculated phase stability and experimentally observed phase and microstructure evolution would test the proposed predictive mechanism.

contradictions.description: The target is presented as the fixed composition Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7, but the intervention and experiment propose varying composition without defining modified compositions; those variants would no longer all be the stated alloy.
